artifacts.notes: The photograph clearly shows a low circular drip pan, central candle socket, candle, and short feet. It does not clearly show a handle: the apparent handled form at the left is a separate object in the crowded display. The listed features are properties of this exemplar only. Background display objects and perspective make the photograph unsuitable as an unedited publication plate. Exact bytes are not retained in the repository.
artifacts.rights_basis: The photographer and uploader, Maximilian775, identifies the image as own work and licenses it under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 on the Wikimedia Commons file page.

edition.title: Bishop Watterson Bugia 1 Museum of Catholic Art and History.jpg

work.author: Maximilian775, photographer
work.description: A documentary photograph of a portable candlestick identified by its museum display card as a bugia from the episcopate of John A. Watterson (1880–1899). The photograph is useful as one dated material witness; it does not establish a universal liturgical morphology.
work.title: Bishop Watterson Bugia at the Museum of Catholic Art and History
